plan: In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors or their bidding behavior. This holds because your payment only depends on the second-highest bid, not your own bid (as long as you win), so overbidding risks paying more than your value and underbidding risks losing profitable wins. With a value of $47, the optimal action is to bid exactly $47 to maximize expected profit.

This is a second-price auction where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy, regardless of what other bidders do. Since I pay the second-highest bid if I win (not my own bid), there's no incentive to shade my bid. Bidding exactly my value of $33 ensures I win whenever the prize is worth more to me than the cost, and I never overpay since I only pay the second-highest bid if I win. This maximizes expected profit.

This is because you pay the second-highest bid (not your own bid) if you win, so there's no incentive to shade your bid up or down. Bidding exactly my value of $36 ensures I win whenever my value exceeds the highest competing bid (profitable), and lose when it doesn't (avoiding a loss). This maximizes expected profit.
